novelty_flags.one_line: The cited arXiv v1 has Proposition 2.1 on monotonicity; pages 35–36 contain Proposition A.4 on irrelevant exposures, not a Proposition 2.2 stating R(G,τ,q)=f_q(H), so the comparator must be re-anchored to its actual conflict-graph claim.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 9–10, Proposition 2.1 and Section 2.3; pp. 34–35, Proposition A.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 2.1 gives only monotonicity in q and G; Section 2.3 defines the single-model conflict graph, while Proposition A.4 at p. 35 concerns zeroing non-relevant exposures. The introduction states only that the minimax risk is a function of the corresponding conflict graph.
For nested exposure models M0⊆M1, the specification-testing minimax error satisfies R*(δ)=1 for every non-trivial separation value.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–7, Sections 3.4 and 4, Theorem 4.7 and Corollary 4.10
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper models exposure-mapping misspecification through exposure-propensity sensitivity bounds and derives partial-identification bounds with orthogonal estimation and rate/inference results.
The paper studies all-treated-versus-none effects and derives minimax rates over all linear estimators and experimental designs under distance-decaying spillovers.
The paper assumes a known exposure mapping and characterizes an assignment distribution and regression-based estimator for worst-case asymptotic variance.
The paper studies two-wave network experiments with local dependence and optimizes participants and treatment assignments for variance of specified estimators.
The Conflict Graph Design targets a pre-specified causal effect with a modified Horvitz–Thompson estimator and variance bound O(λ(H)/n).
The article studies design-based causal inference under arbitrary and network interference and establishes its nonconcentration limitation benchmark.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace every reference to Kandiros–Harshaw–Sävje Proposition 2.2 and Appendix A.5 with the actual Section 2.3/introductory claim, explicitly state that the paper supplies single-model graph-based minimax analysis rather than the claimed exact proposition, and narrow the non-representability comparison accordingly.

Elevate the persistent witness from an engineered common-selector example to a stated generic obstruction class, such as a family of exposure-menu incidence structures closed under replication, and prove the graph multiset cannot determine risk throughout that class.
Give the structural-compression question a concrete algorithmic target: specify a menu/incidence class, input encoding, certificate factor, and polynomial runtime or hardness alternative.

recommended_next_step: Correct and re-anchor the Kandiros comparison, then retain the finite-menu saddle and persistent cross-model non-representability kernel for Stage 0 at field-tier scope.
